dct_description_sm: Many emerged sea-level indicators have been recorded on Baffin Island, NU, however there is little knowledge of the submerged sea-level indicators within the near-shore fjord systems and coastline. Due to the retreat of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, the Canadian Arctic has been undergoing glacial isostatic rebound, which continues to create regions of uplift and some of subsidence. The boundary between presently emerging and submerging landmasses can be found running close to the coastline of eastern Baffin Island. This indicates that in some regions of the easternmost coast sea-level indictors are submerged due to continuous subsidence during the postglacial period. It is therefore the purpose of this project to explore and map submerged sea-level indictors within the near-shore coastline of the Cumberland Peninsula, Baffin Island.  With these geomorphic features mapped and analyzed, the palaeo-sea-level can be determined and recorded as baseline data to support projections of future sea levels under various climate-change scenarios. This will contribute to a better understanding of the crustal response to complex glacial loading and unloading patterns for this region and help to refine local sea-level projections for coastal communities.
dct_title_s: Submerged postglacial sea-level record of Eastern Baffin Island
